doc.title: Billie Pierce and De De Pierce Interview, 1959-10-07

title: Ernest's in-laws Frank Crump and Henry Julian
summary: He names his musical brothers-in-law, Frank Crump's death and Ernest Crump on banjo.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Did you, uh, have any musicians in your family?
No. He was my brother-in-law, but my wife's brother, Frank Crump. Who was he? And another brother-in-law, Henry Julian, saxophones.
Frank used to play clarinet and saxophone. Yeah, and little Frank, little Frank Crump, little brother just about like that.
Had a pretty bush of hell. Oh, when I was taking, uh, I was going to radio school then. How long Frank been there? Frank been there about- About eight years?
Yeah, but I'm on around about eight years. About eight years.

Taking sick, taking sick on the bus, some of the bus coming off a job. And they rushed him right back, right to the hospital next morning, he was dead. Yeah. Frank was- Yeah, it was short for, but his daddy was a old time musician. You know, but he didn't read his dad, but Frank read. Ernest Crump, that was his dad, well he's dead too.
What did he play, bass though?
No, I used to play a banjo.
Ernest Crump was a banjo? Yeah, banjo. Did you all work with him ever, Ernest Crump?
No, he was much older than Dean, man.
I just knew his son, Crump. I did play a job. Maybe you did. I did, I did.
Oh yeah, didn't y'all go across the river one time? When he got in, when he got in an accident. When he got in an accident. When he got in an accident. He was in a wreck together, yeah.
That's right. That's right. He was in a wreck together.
He was in a wreck together.
He went on the water, more to the river.
Yeah, that's right. That was my banjo he had with him then. He busted up. He was in a wreck together.
